name: Anguilla (Republic, 1967–1969)
description: A white field with a light-blue stripe along the base, charged with three orange dolphins leaping in a circle.
history: The Dolphin Flag was adopted on 29 September 1967 by the Republic of Anguilla, proclaimed after the island rejected inclusion in the Associated State of Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla; it replaced the short-lived Mermaid flag. Its design is variously credited to Marvin Oberman and Lydia Gumbs or to Mike Young. British rule was restored on 19 March 1969, though the flag stayed in unofficial use and its dolphins survive in Anguilla's present arms.
